newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Foreign funds boost investment in Colombian stocks.
newsitem.headline: Foreign funds boost investment in Colombian stocks.

text.p: Foreign investment funds have increased their Colombian shareholdings by 24.7 percent in real peso terms so far this year, the Securities Superintendency reported on Thursday.
It said foreign funds held the equivalent of $1.05 billion in Colombian shares as of October 31, up from $854.9 million on the same date last year. The increase in dollar terms is 23.3 percent.

Between September 30 and October 31, foreign funds inccreased their portfolio investment in Colombia by 1.9 percent, the Superintendency said, adding that the 15 funds authorized to purchase Colombian ADRs or GDRs had an accumulated investment of $492 million as of October 31.

The political crisis stemming from charges that President Ernesto Samper used millions of dollars in drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign hurt the Colombian stock market earlier this year and recovery so far, against the backdrop of continuing tension in the country's ties with Washington, has been slow.
Some analysts believe the market's recovery will gather momentum in the coming months, however, as increased oil income and a drop in domestic interest rates help fuel an economic rebound in 1997.
